BEHAVIORAL CHANGE vs OLD THROTTLE (v5 server-throttle, request 4 trigger)
  - standard LinUCB: unchanged lock-in (dominant decrease-concurrency no-op, unique 1.0).
  - periodic LinUCB: CHANGED. In v5 its dominant arm was decrease-chunk-size; here it is
    increase-concurrency and it raises concurrency to ~3.9, closing most of the gap to
    concurrency-adaptive (new 1323ms vs 1325ms). Under the old request-count throttle,
    increasing concurrency did not help because the 4-request trigger had already fired.
